rationale: The workflow already implements the workflow-level optimizations supported by the retrieved evidence, so no new change preserves coverage while adding benefit. Dependency downloads are already cached via `actions/setup-node` with `cache: npm` (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE; an equivalent cache already exists, which is a listed contraindication). The job is already bounded by a custom `timeout-minutes: 20` versus the default, satisfying P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT; the only measured experiment for that pattern added a timeout to a job that had none (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508), and lowering the existing 20-minute limit is not supported without cold-run/slow-run validation (contraindication: valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit). Superseded-run cancellation is already present via `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE), and path filtering is already present via `paths-ignore` (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER). The remaining patterns are not applicable: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST), no scheduled triggers (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no Bazel build (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), and test selection/prioritization/build selection (P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT) would reduce required-check coverage and is contraindicated for required checks. Therefore no supported optimization is both applicable and coverage-preserving.
